title: docs(fields): grid column examples use only declared column keys
body:
Fixes #10406
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`content/docs/fields/grid.mdx` stops teaching four grid-column keys that no column shape declares. One file, docs only.

| Key on the page | Declared? (read at base `cc139d820`, `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 as installed per the lockfile) | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `currency: 'USD'` (Column Types example) | No: absent from `GridColumn` (`packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.tsx`), from `GridColumnDefinition` (`packages/types/src/field-types.ts`) and from the strict `InlineGridColumnSchema` | Dropped. One sentence added under the block: a `currency` column has no currency key of its own and its cells are shown in the tenant's default currency. |
| `min: 1` (Column Types example; Invoice Line Items) | No: none of the three faces declares `min` (`GridColumnDefinition` only has a nested `validate`, which the spec schema refuses) | Dropped, both places. |
| `readonly: true` (Invoice amount; Order total) | No. The declared read-only spellings are `computed` + `expr` and `readonlyWhen`, on both `GridColumn` and `InlineGridColumnSchema` | Invoice `amount` rewritten to `computed: true, expr: 'quantity * unit_price'`, the pattern the `GridColumn.computed` doc comment names. Order `total` dropped: a formula there would run over the `discount` column, whose `type: 'percent'` is itself undeclared (see Acceptance notes), so no formula was invented. |
| `reference_to: 'products'` (Order Details lookup) | No. `GridColumn` and `InlineGridColumnSchema` both declare `reference` ("Referenced object for `type: 'lookup'` cells") | Rewritten to `reference: 'products'`. |

On the triage suggestion to say that a fixed currency comes from the field's `currencyConfig`: it was not written, because it is not true of a grid column today. `columnCurrency` in `GridField.tsx` passes no field-level leg to `resolveFieldCurrency` and lands on the tenant default, and the column derivation copies no currency key from the child field. So the page now says what the widget does. No new key is declared anywhere.

## Pin: none added, one-off probe instead

No existing docs-conformance test parses the column literals on this page. The per-page doc tests (for example `calendar-doc-key-set-8830.test.ts`) are each their own file, and none reads `fields/grid.mdx`. Per the dispatch, no new infrastructure was built. A one-off probe pulled every `{ name: … }` literal inside a `columns: [` block on the page, evaluated it (an `options: [...]` placeholder was replaced by one option) and ran it through the installed `InlineGridColumnSchema.safeParse`. The two `field`-keyed `ListColumn` entries in the `object-grid` block were skipped because they are a different schema. Control leg in the same run: a column carrying `currency` is refused, and the same column without it parses.

- Before (base `cc139d820`): 24 literals · 13 pass · 11 fail
- After (head `2bd9985d5`): 24 literals · 19 pass · 5 fail

The six failures that cleared are exactly the four named keys: `currency` ×1, `min` ×2, `readonly` ×2, `reference_to` ×1. The five that remain are outside this card; they are listed below.

## Acceptance notes

- **Remaining probe failures (not touched here):** `type: 'boolean'` ×2, `type: 'percent'` ×1 and `type: 'user'` ×1 fail as `invalid_value` on `type`, because the declared column type union has nine members and these are not among them. The sentence "Columns can use any field type" above the example says the opposite. `defaultValue: 1` in the typed `GridFieldMetadata` example fails `unrecognized_keys`. `GridColumnDefinition` declares it, but the spec schema refuses it and `GridField` never reads it.
- **Two objectui faces disagree:** `GridColumnDefinition` (`@object-ui/types`) declares `defaultValue` and `validate`, which the spec refuses. It also lacks `reference`, `options`, `computed`, `expr` and the other keys that `GridColumn` and the spec both declare, and it types `type` as a bare string. `GridColumn` and `InlineGridColumnSchema` agree on `reference`, so the dispatch's hypothesis that the two spell a lookup target differently did not hold. The faces were not reconciled here.
- The page's "Validation" snippet still reads `col.min` off a user-defined `ColumnDefinition`. It is custom code, not a column literal, and it was left alone.
- Other pages under `content/docs/fields/`: no column-level `currency` key. The only `currency: '…'` hit is `currency.mdx`'s field-level `CurrencyFieldMetadata` example, which declares it (that hit doubles as the grep's positive control).

## Gates (head `2bd9985d5`)

Derived by hand from `package.json` and the workflows whose paths cover `content/**`. Exit codes were written to files before they were read.

- `check-control-bytes` 0 · `check-doc-component-types` 0 · `check-prompt-component-keys` 0 · `check-doc-example-ids` 0 · `check-doc-fence-languages` 0 · `check-doc-links` 0 · `check:docs-route-closure` 0
- `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` 0 ("0 new citation(s)")
- `check-changeset-presence` 0 ("no changeset is owed": a docs-only diff, so no changeset was added)
- NOT MEASURED: `check-doc-snippet-types` / `check-doc-example-types`. Both need the built `dist` closure, and the diff touches no `ts`/`tsx` fence (only `plaintext` fences and prose), so CI owns them. External link check (`check-links.yml`): not run, because the diff adds no link.

Not a governed surface. Dispatched: stays draft for the seat.
